1	# Releasing Hey Reachy
2	
3	Signed artifacts are produced locally; CI only publishes the GitHub release with
4	generated notes. Credentials never enter the repository or CI.
5	
6	## One-time setup
7	
8	1. **App Store Connect API key** — App Store Connect → Users and Access →
9	   Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys, role **App Manager**.
10	   Download the `.p8` once and write the credentials file:
11	
12	   ```bash
13	   mkdir -p ~/.config/reachy-mini
14	   cat > ~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env <<'CONF'
15	   REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX
16	   REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX
17	   REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
18	   REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH=/Users/you/.config/reachy-mini/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8
19	   CONF
20	   ```
21	
22	2. **App IDs and the App Group** — the first signed build with
23	   `-allowProvisioningUpdates` registers the bundle ids
24	   (`com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`, `.Widget`), but the
25	   `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini` capability must be added by hand in
26	   Xcode's Signing & Capabilities, once per App ID (app and widget separately,
27	   iOS and macOS separately). `xcodebuild` cannot create it.
28	
29	3. **App Store Connect app record** — My Apps → New App:
30	   - Name: **Hey Reachy**; if taken, fall back to “Hey Reachy — robot remote”.
31	   - Subtitle: **Control your Reachy Mini**.
32	   - Bundle id `com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`.
33	   - The description must state it is an unofficial client for Reachy Mini by
34	     Pollen Robotics. A public TestFlight link goes through Beta App Review, so
35	     the name is checked before any App Store submission.
36	   - App Privacy: no data collected. The app talks to the robot on the local
37	     network and to Hugging Face with the user's own OAuth session; nothing is
38	     sent to the developer.
39	   - Encryption: answered in the Info.plist (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`),
40	     ASC asks nothing per build.
41	
42	4. **Developer ID Application certificate** (macOS) — Xcode → Settings →
43	   Accounts → Manage Certificates → “+” → Developer ID Application.
44

# Releasing Hey Reachy

Signed artifacts are produced locally; CI only publishes the GitHub release with
generated notes. Credentials never enter the repository or CI.

## One-time setup

1. **App Store Connect API key** — App Store Connect → Users and Access →
   Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys, role **App Manager**.
   Download the `.p8` once and write the credentials file:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.config/reachy-mini
   cat > ~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env <<'CONF'
   REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX
   REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX
   REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
   REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH=/Users/you/.config/reachy-mini/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8
   CONF
   ```

2. **App IDs and the App Group** — the first signed build with
   `-allowProvisioningUpdates` registers the bundle ids
   (`com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`, `.Widget`), but the
   `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini` capability must be added by hand in
   Xcode's Signing & Capabilities, once per App ID (app and widget separately,
   iOS and macOS separately). `xcodebuild` cannot create it.

3. **App Store Connect app record** — My Apps → New App:
   - Name: **Hey Reachy**; if taken, fall back to “Hey Reachy — robot remote”.
   - Subtitle: **Control your Reachy Mini**.
   - Bundle id `com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`.
   - The description must state it is an unofficial client for Reachy Mini by
     Pollen Robotics. A public TestFlight link goes through Beta App Review, so
     the name is checked before any App Store submission.
   - App Privacy: no data collected. The app talks to the robot on the local
     network and to Hugging Face with the user's own OAuth session; nothing is
     sent to the developer.
   - Encryption: answered in the Info.plist (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`),
     ASC asks nothing per build.

4. **Developer ID Application certificate** (macOS) — Xcode → Settings →
   Accounts → Manage Certificates → “+” → Developer ID Application.

## Each release

1. Bump `MARKETING_VERSION` in `Apps/Project.swift` (bare semver, e.g. `0.2.0`)
   and land it on `main`. Build numbers are the commit count — nothing to bump.
2. Tag and push; the tag triggers the GitHub release with git-cliff notes:

   ```bash
   git tag 0.2.0 && git push origin 0.2.0
   ```

3. Produce and ship the artifacts:

   ```bash
   mise run release:ios     # archive → TestFlight
   mise run release:macos   # archive → Developer ID → notarize → staple → zip
   gh release upload 0.2.0 Apps/DerivedData/Export/macOS/HeyReachy-0.2.0.zip
   ```

Dry runs: `mise run release:ios -- --no-upload` exports an `.ipa` without
uploading; `mise run release:macos -- --no-notarize` stops after the signed
export.

## Querying App Store Connect

`mise run asc` is the App Store Connect CLI with the same key already loaded —
`Scripts/asc.sh` maps the `REACHY_ASC_*` values onto the `ASC_*` names the tool
reads, so nothing is stored twice and no keychain profile exists to drift.

```bash
mise run asc -- apps list
mise run asc -- builds list --app 6799644194   # did the TestFlight upload land?
mise run asc -- testflight beta-groups list --app 6799644194
```

run by hand silently outranks this wrapper — `mise run asc -- auth status`

same limit release-ios.sh documents applies: it can read and submit, and it
cannot manage provisioning profiles.

commit) covering TestFlight, metadata, submissions and signing.

Xcode Cloud: it installs the pinned tools through the committed `bin/mise`
bootstrap, generates the workspace, and stamps `CI_BUILD_NUMBER` in as the
build number. Signing there is managed by Apple — no certificates leave the
account — and TestFlight distribution is a post-action checkbox. The setup
quirks (create the workflow from a local Xcode, start the build counter above
the last local upload, Git LFS is unsupported so never build the snapshot

#!/bin/bash
# Archive the iOS app (Release, signed) and upload it to TestFlight.
#
#   mise run release:ios              # archive → upload to App Store Connect
#   mise run release:ios -- --no-upload   # archive → export an .ipa locally
#
# Signing and uploading go through the Xcode account, not the App Store Connect
# API key — see release-env.sh for the measurement behind that.
#
# The build number is the commit count: monotonic, reproducible, and never
# stored in the repository — so releasing does not require a version-bump
# commit for anything but MARKETING_VERSION.
set -euo pipefail

# shellcheck source=Scripts/release-env.sh
. "$(dirname "$0")/release-env.sh"

upload=true
require_development_team
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
  --no-upload) upload=false ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: release-ios.sh [--no-upload]" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
  esac
  shift
done

BUILD_NUMBER="$(git rev-list --count HEAD)"
ARCHIVE=Apps/DerivedData/Archives/ReachyMini-iOS.xcarchive

set -o pipefail
xcodebuild archive \
  -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -configuration Release \
  -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
  CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$BUILD_NUMBER" \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  2>&1 | xcsift

EXPORT_OPTIONS=Scripts/exportOptions/appstore.plist
if [ "$upload" = false ]; then
  # Same options with the upload turned into a local export.
  EXPORT_OPTIONS="$(mktemp -t reachy-export-options).plist"
  plutil -convert xml1 -o "$EXPORT_OPTIONS" Scripts/exportOptions/appstore.plist
  plutil -replace destination -string export "$EXPORT_OPTIONS"
fi

xcodebuild -exportArchive \
  -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" \
  -exportOptionsPlist "$EXPORT_OPTIONS" \
  -exportPath Apps/DerivedData/Export/iOS \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  2>&1 | xcsift

if [ "$upload" = true ]; then
  echo "Uploaded build $BUILD_NUMBER to App Store Connect. TestFlight shows it after processing (minutes)."
else
  echo "Exported without uploading:"
  ls Apps/DerivedData/Export/iOS/*.ipa
fi

#!/bin/bash
# Archive the macOS app (Release, signed), export it with Developer ID,
# notarize, staple, and zip it for distribution.
#
#   mise run release:macos               # the whole pipeline
#   mise run release:macos -- --no-notarize  # stop after the signed export
#
# Needs a "Developer ID Application" certificate in the keychain
# (Xcode → Settings → Accounts → Manage Certificates) besides the ASC API key.
set -euo pipefail

# shellcheck source=Scripts/release-env.sh
. "$(dirname "$0")/release-env.sh"

notarize=true
require_development_team
require_asc_key
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
  --no-notarize) notarize=false ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: release-macos.sh [--no-notarize]" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
  esac
  shift
done

BUILD_NUMBER="$(git rev-list --count HEAD)"
ARCHIVE=Apps/DerivedData/Archives/ReachyMini-macOS.xcarchive
EXPORT_DIR=Apps/DerivedData/Export/macOS

set -o pipefail
xcodebuild archive \
  -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
  -destination 'generic/platform=macOS' -configuration Release \
  -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
  CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$BUILD_NUMBER" \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  2>&1 | xcsift

/bin/rm -rf "$EXPORT_DIR"
xcodebuild -exportArchive \
  -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" \
  -exportOptionsPlist Scripts/exportOptions/developer-id.plist \
  -exportPath "$EXPORT_DIR" \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  2>&1 | xcsift

APP="$EXPORT_DIR/ReachyMini.app"
VERSION="$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :CFBundleShortVersionString' "$APP/Contents/Info.plist")"
ZIP="$EXPORT_DIR/HeyReachy-$VERSION.zip"

ditto -c -k --keepParent "$APP" "$ZIP"

if [ "$notarize" = true ]; then
  xcrun notarytool submit "$ZIP" \
    --key "$REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH" \
    --key-id "$REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID" \
    --issuer "$REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID" \
    --wait
  xcrun stapler staple "$APP"
  # The staple changed the bundle, so the zip that ships is rebuilt from it.
  /bin/rm "$ZIP"
  ditto -c -k --keepParent "$APP" "$ZIP"
  echo "Notarized and stapled. Attach it to the tag's GitHub release with:"
else
  echo "Signed but NOT notarized (--no-notarize). For a real release rerun without the flag."
fi
echo "  gh release upload $VERSION $ZIP"

  connecting to one from the simulator. A stand-in advert for discovery work is one command:
  `dns-sd -R reachy_mini _reachy-mini._tcp local 8000 unit_id=<hex>`, and a second registration of the same instance
  name comes back as `reachy_mini (2)`.

  correctly reports nothing.

  prompt, detect denial via timeout, and deep-link to Settings.

  use blanket `NSExceptionDomains`.

  limitation in connection UI and never encourage public routing/port forwarding.

## Robot facts

- Wireless AP mode (out of box): SSID `reachy-mini-ap`, password `reachy-mini`, robot IP `10.42.0.1`.

Отсюда два скрипта и два архива — `ReachyMini-iOS.xcarchive` и `ReachyMini-macOS.xcarchive` — из **одного и того же** таргета `Project.swift:45`.
- «Три платформы» в терминах App Store Connect — это две: iPhone и iPad живут под одной платформой iOS (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1,2`), macOS — отдельная.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Так что вы правы наполовину, и вторая половина интереснее: **запись в ASC уже двухплатформенная**.

```
│ 2c1da4c4-… │ 1.0 │ macOS │ PREPARE_FOR_SUBMISSION │
│ 2d312612-… │ 1.0 │ iOS   │ PREPARE_FOR_SUBMISSION │
```

| | iOS (`appstore.plist`) | macOS (`developer-id.plist`) |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `app-store-connect` | `developer-id` |
| `destination` | `upload` | `export` |
| Куда приезжает | TestFlight | zip → нотаризация → GitHub Release |

Это осознанный выбор канала, а не недоделка: macOS-таргет уже подписан под Developer ID (`ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME[sdk=macosx*] = YES`, `Project.swift:139`) и прогоняется через `notarytool` + `stapler`. Причём песочница у него **уже включена** — в `ReachyMini-macOS.entitlements` лежит `com.apple.security.app-sandbox`, `network.client`, `device.audio-input`, `device.bluetooth` и App Group. Это самое дорогое требование Mac App Store, и оно уже выполнено.

Чтобы macOS поехал в TestFlight, нужно:

1. Второй export-plist с `method = app-store-connect` — на выходе будет **`.pkg`**, а не `.app`/zip.
2. Сертификат **Apple Distribution** + Mac App Store профиль вместо Developer ID (`-allowProvisioningUpdates` заведёт профиль, но сам сертификат — руками в Xcode, как и Developer ID по `docs/release.md:42`).
3. Зарегистрировать App Group на **macOS-овском** App ID — `docs/release.md:22` уже предупреждает, что это делается отдельно для iOS и macOS и `xcodebuild` этого не умеет.
4. Нотаризация из этой ветки уходит — App Store подписывает и нотаризует у себя.

**Развилка, которую стоит решить вам, а не мне.** Каналы не взаимоисключающие — один архив можно экспортировать дважды, и `release-macos.sh` естественно превращается в `--channel appstore|developer-id|both`. Но выбор имеет цену:

- **Только Mac App Store** — тестировщики ставят из TestFlight в один клик, никакого Gatekeeper. Цена: ревью (а это неофициальный клиент к чужому железу — по описанию из `docs/release.md:33` вопросы возможны) и потеря возможности выкатить сборку мгновенно.
- **Только Developer ID** (как сейчас) — zip раздаётся кому угодно и когда угодно, ревью нет. Цена: пользователь качает файл с GitHub, macOS-сборки нет в TestFlight рядом с iOS.
- **Оба** — честно лучший вариант по покрытию, но это два сертификата, два экспорта и два места, куда смотреть при разборе бага.

Моя рекомендация — **оба**, с флагом в скрипте: запись в ASC под macOS уже создана и сейчас просто простаивает, а песочница — главный барьер — уже пройдена, так что инкремент невелик.

2	# Sourced by release-ios.sh, release-macos.sh and asc.sh: loads and checks the
3	# release credentials. Like the device signing team, they live outside every worktree in
4	# ~/.config/reachy-mini/, so nothing is copied when a workspace is created and
5	# nothing account-specific ever lands in the repository.
6	#
7	# Exported variables win over the file, so a CI machine can inject its own.
8	
9	RELEASE_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/reachy-mini/release.env"
10	DEVICE_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/reachy-mini/device.env"
11	
12	# The signing team is the same one device builds already use; read it first so
13	# release.env only has to add the App Store Connect key.
14	if [ -z "${REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ] && [ -f "$DEVICE_CONFIG" ]; then
15	  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
16	  . "$DEVICE_CONFIG"
17	fi
18	if [ -f "$RELEASE_CONFIG" ]; then
19	  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
20	  . "$RELEASE_CONFIG"
21	fi
22	
23	# Demanded by the two scripts that archive; asc.sh sources this file for the API key
24	# alone and never signs anything, so the check cannot run on load.
25	require_development_team() {
26	  [ -n "${REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ] && return 0
27	  cat >&2 <<EOF
28	No signing team. Write it once, the way device builds already expect:
29	
30	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$DEVICE_CONFIG")"
31	  echo 'REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX' > "$DEVICE_CONFIG"
32	
33	The id is in Xcode → Settings → Accounts, next to the team that owns com.alexey1312.*.
34	EOF
35	  exit 1
36	}
37	
38	# The API key is optional, and deliberately unused for signing. xcodebuild takes
39	# `-authenticationKey*` as "do everything through cloud signing", and a key below
40	# the Admin role cannot manage profiles — the export then fails with "Cloud
41	# signing permission error" and "No profiles were found" even though the
42	# certificate is right there in the keychain. A key's role cannot be changed
43	# after it is created. Without the flags xcodebuild uses the Xcode account, which
44	# has the rights, so signing is left to it and the key is kept for the two things
45	# that only need to read and submit: notarization, and CI.
46	REACHY_HAS_ASC=""
47	if [ -n "${REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID:-}" ] && [ -n "${REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID:-}" ] && [ -n "${REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH:-}" ]; then
48	  if [ ! -f "$REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH" ]; then
49	    echo "REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH points at $REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH, which does not exist." >&2
50	    exit 1
51	  fi
52	  REACHY_HAS_ASC=1
53	fi
54	
55	# Called by the macOS script, where notarytool has no other way in, and by asc.sh,
56	# which is nothing but the key.

58	  [ -n "$REACHY_HAS_ASC" ] && return 0
59	  cat >&2 <<EOF
60	This needs an App Store Connect API key (App Store Connect → Users and Access →
61	Integrations → App Store Connect API). Write the three values once:
62	
63	  cat >> "$RELEASE_CONFIG" <<'CONF'
64	REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX
65	REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
66	REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH=$HOME/.config/reachy-mini/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8
67	CONF
68	
69	The one-time App Store Connect setup is documented in docs/release.md.
70	EOF
71	  exit 1
72	}

# Sourced by release-ios.sh, release-macos.sh and asc.sh: loads and checks the
# release credentials. Like the device signing team, they live outside every worktree in
# ~/.config/reachy-mini/, so nothing is copied when a workspace is created and
# nothing account-specific ever lands in the repository.
#
# Exported variables win over the file, so a CI machine can inject its own.

RELEASE_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/reachy-mini/release.env"
DEVICE_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/reachy-mini/device.env"

# The signing team is the same one device builds already use; read it first so
# release.env only has to add the App Store Connect key.
if [ -z "${REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ] && [ -f "$DEVICE_CONFIG" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$DEVICE_CONFIG"
fi
if [ -f "$RELEASE_CONFIG" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$RELEASE_CONFIG"
fi

# Demanded by the two scripts that archive; asc.sh sources this file for the API key
# alone and never signs anything, so the check cannot run on load.
require_development_team() {
  [ -n "${REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ] && return 0
  cat >&2 <<EOF
No signing team. Write it once, the way device builds already expect:

  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$DEVICE_CONFIG")"
  echo 'REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX' > "$DEVICE_CONFIG"

The id is in Xcode → Settings → Accounts, next to the team that owns com.alexey1312.*.
EOF
  exit 1
}

# The API key is optional, and deliberately unused for signing. xcodebuild takes
# `-authenticationKey*` as "do everything through cloud signing", and a key below
# the Admin role cannot manage profiles — the export then fails with "Cloud
# signing permission error" and "No profiles were found" even though the
# certificate is right there in the keychain. A key's role cannot be changed
# after it is created. Without the flags xcodebuild uses the Xcode account, which
# has the rights, so signing is left to it and the key is kept for the two things
# that only need to read and submit: notarization, and CI.
REACHY_HAS_ASC=""
if [ -n "${REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID:-}" ] && [ -n "${REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID:-}" ] && [ -n "${REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH:-}" ]; then
  if [ ! -f "$REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH" ]; then
    echo "REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH points at $REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH, which does not exist." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  REACHY_HAS_ASC=1
fi

# Called by the macOS script, where notarytool has no other way in, and by asc.sh,
# which is nothing but the key.
require_asc_key() {
  [ -n "$REACHY_HAS_ASC" ] && return 0
  cat >&2 <<EOF
This needs an App Store Connect API key (App Store Connect → Users and Access →
Integrations → App Store Connect API). Write the three values once:

  cat >> "$RELEASE_CONFIG" <<'CONF'
REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX
REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH=$HOME/.config/reachy-mini/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8
CONF

The one-time App Store Connect setup is documented in docs/release.md.
EOF
  exit 1
}

Значит Mac App Store-экспорт пойдёт ровно тем же механизмом, что уже работает для iOS.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Отдельный plist для macOS не нужен: `method = app-store-connect` не привязан к платформе, и `Scripts/exportOptions/appstore.plist` подходит обоим архивам как есть. Разница между iOS и macOS в этом канале — только в том, что на выходе `.ipa` против `.pkg`, а это решает сам `-exportArchive` по SDK архива.

`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Начну с общего хелпера, чтобы трюк «выгрузить против выгрузить-локально» не размножился в два скрипта.

#!/bin/bash
# Archive the macOS app (Release, signed) and ship it through both distribution
# channels: the Mac App Store (TestFlight) and Developer ID (notarized zip).
#
#   mise run release:macos                             # both channels
#   mise run release:macos -- --channel appstore       # TestFlight only
#   mise run release:macos -- --channel developer-id   # notarized zip only
#   mise run release:macos -- --no-notarize            # developer-id: stop after signing
#   mise run release:macos -- --no-upload              # appstore: export a .pkg locally
#
# The last two flags each belong to one channel and are ignored by the other.
#
# One archive feeds both exports: it is not signed for a channel, `-exportArchive`
# re-signs it per method, so the two artifacts cannot differ in anything but the
# signature. Developer ID runs first deliberately — it is the artifact that always
# ships, and an App Store upload that fails should not also cost you the zip.
#
# Needs a "Developer ID Application" certificate in the keychain
# (Xcode → Settings → Accounts → Manage Certificates) besides the ASC API key.
set -euo pipefail

# shellcheck source=Scripts/release-env.sh
. "$(dirname "$0")/release-env.sh"

channel=both
notarize=true
upload=true
require_development_team
usage() {
  echo "usage: release-macos.sh [--channel appstore|developer-id|both] [--no-notarize] [--no-upload]" >&2
  exit 2
}
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
  --channel)
    shift
    case "${1:-}" in
    appstore | developer-id | both) channel="$1" ;;
    *) usage ;;
    esac
    ;;
  --no-notarize) notarize=false ;;
  --no-upload) upload=false ;;
  *) usage ;;
  esac
  shift
done

wants_appstore=false
wants_developer_id=false
[ "$channel" = appstore ] || [ "$channel" = both ] && wants_appstore=true
[ "$channel" = developer-id ] || [ "$channel" = both ] && wants_developer_id=true

# Only notarization needs the key; the App Store channel signs through the Xcode
# account like the iOS one, for the reason release-env.sh documents.
if [ "$wants_developer_id" = true ] && [ "$notarize" = true ]; then
  require_asc_key
fi

BUILD_NUMBER="$(git rev-list --count HEAD)"
ARCHIVE=Apps/DerivedData/Archives/ReachyMini-macOS.xcarchive
EXPORT_DIR=Apps/DerivedData/Export/macOS

set -o pipefail
xcodebuild archive \
  -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
  -destination 'generic/platform=macOS' -configuration Release \
  -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
  CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$BUILD_NUMBER" \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  2>&1 | xcsift

if [ "$wants_developer_id" = true ]; then
  /bin/rm -rf "$EXPORT_DIR/DeveloperID"
  xcodebuild -exportArchive \
    -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" \
    -exportOptionsPlist Scripts/exportOptions/developer-id.plist \
    -exportPath "$EXPORT_DIR/DeveloperID" \
    -allowProvisioningUpdates \
    2>&1 | xcsift

  APP="$EXPORT_DIR/DeveloperID/ReachyMini.app"
  VERSION="$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :CFBundleShortVersionString' "$APP/Contents/Info.plist")"
  # The zip stays at the top of the export directory: it is the one artifact that
  # leaves this machine by hand, and docs/release.md names that path.
  ZIP="$EXPORT_DIR/HeyReachy-$VERSION.zip"

  /bin/rm -f "$ZIP"
  ditto -c -k --keepParent "$APP" "$ZIP"

  if [ "$notarize" = true ]; then
    xcrun notarytool submit "$ZIP" \
      --key "$REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH" \
      --key-id "$REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID" \
      --issuer "$REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID" \
      --wait
    xcrun stapler staple "$APP"
    # The staple changed the bundle, so the zip that ships is rebuilt from it.
    /bin/rm "$ZIP"
    ditto -c -k --keepParent "$APP" "$ZIP"
    echo "Notarized and stapled. Attach it to the tag's GitHub release with:"
  else
    echo "Signed but NOT notarized (--no-notarize). For a real release rerun without the flag."
  fi
  echo "  gh release upload $VERSION $ZIP"
fi

if [ "$wants_appstore" = true ]; then
  /bin/rm -rf "$EXPORT_DIR/AppStore"
  xcodebuild -exportArchive \
    -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" \
    -exportOptionsPlist "$(appstore_export_options "$upload")" \
    -exportPath "$EXPORT_DIR/AppStore" \
    -allowProvisioningUpdates \
    2>&1 | xcsift

  if [ "$upload" = true ]; then
    echo "Uploaded macOS build $BUILD_NUMBER to App Store Connect. TestFlight shows it after processing (minutes)."
  else
    echo "Exported without uploading:"
    ls "$EXPORT_DIR/AppStore"/*.pkg
  fi
fi

# Releasing Hey Reachy

Signed artifacts are produced locally; CI only publishes the GitHub release with
generated notes. Credentials never enter the repository or CI.

## One-time setup

1. **App Store Connect API key** — App Store Connect → Users and Access →
   Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys, role **App Manager**.
   Download the `.p8` once and write the credentials file:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.config/reachy-mini
   cat > ~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env <<'CONF'
   REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX
   REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX
   REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
   REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH=/Users/you/.config/reachy-mini/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8
   CONF
   ```

2. **App IDs and the App Group** — the first signed build with
   `-allowProvisioningUpdates` registers the bundle ids
   (`com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`, `.Widget`), but the
   `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini` capability must be added by hand in
   Xcode's Signing & Capabilities, once per App ID (app and widget separately,
   iOS and macOS separately). `xcodebuild` cannot create it.

3. **App Store Connect app record** — My Apps → New App:
   - Name: **Hey Reachy**; if taken, fall back to “Hey Reachy — robot remote”.
   - Subtitle: **Control your Reachy Mini**.
   - Bundle id `com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`.
   - The description must state it is an unofficial client for Reachy Mini by
     Pollen Robotics. A public TestFlight link goes through Beta App Review, so
     the name is checked before any App Store submission.
   - App Privacy: no data collected. The app talks to the robot on the local
     network and to Hugging Face with the user's own OAuth session; nothing is
     sent to the developer.
   - Encryption: answered in the Info.plist (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`),
     ASC asks nothing per build.

4. **Developer ID Application certificate** (macOS) — Xcode → Settings →
   Accounts → Manage Certificates → “+” → Developer ID Application.

## Each release

1. Bump `MARKETING_VERSION` in `Apps/Project.swift` (bare semver, e.g. `0.2.0`)
   and land it on `main`. Build numbers are the commit count — nothing to bump.
2. Tag and push; the tag triggers the GitHub release with git-cliff notes:

   ```bash
   git tag 0.2.0 && git push origin 0.2.0
   ```

3. Produce and ship the artifacts:

   ```bash
   mise run release:ios     # archive → TestFlight
   mise run release:macos   # archive → Developer ID → notarize → staple → zip
   gh release upload 0.2.0 Apps/DerivedData/Export/macOS/HeyReachy-0.2.0.zip
   ```

Dry runs: `mise run release:ios -- --no-upload` exports an `.ipa` without
uploading; `mise run release:macos -- --no-notarize` stops after the signed
export.

## Querying App Store Connect

`mise run asc` is the App Store Connect CLI with the same key already loaded —
`Scripts/asc.sh` maps the `REACHY_ASC_*` values onto the `ASC_*` names the tool
reads, so nothing is stored twice and no keychain profile exists to drift.
Everything after `--` goes to `asc`:

```bash
mise run asc -- apps list
mise run asc -- builds list --app 6799644194   # did the TestFlight upload land?
mise run asc -- testflight beta-groups list --app 6799644194
```

`asc` resolves a stored profile before the environment, so an `asc auth login`
run by hand silently outranks this wrapper — `mise run asc -- auth status`
prints which of the two is answering. The key is App Manager, not Admin, so the
same limit release-ios.sh documents applies: it can read and submit, and it
cannot manage provisioning profiles.

The CLI also ships 23 agent skills (`asc install-skills`, pinned to a reviewed
commit) covering TestFlight, metadata, submissions and signing.

## Xcode Cloud (optional, continuous TestFlight)

`Apps/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh` makes a generated project buildable on
Xcode Cloud: it installs the pinned tools through the committed `bin/mise`
bootstrap, generates the workspace, and stamps `CI_BUILD_NUMBER` in as the
build number. Signing there is managed by Apple — no certificates leave the
account — and TestFlight distribution is a post-action checkbox. The setup
quirks (create the workflow from a local Xcode, start the build counter above
the last local upload, Git LFS is unsupported so never build the snapshot
scheme there) are commented at the top of the script.

**Что изменилось в коде**

`Scripts/release-macos.sh` — один архив, два экспорта, флаг `--channel appstore|developer-id|both` (по умолчанию `both`). Developer ID идёт первым намеренно: это артефакт, который всегда отгружается, и провалившаяся загрузка в App Store не должна вдобавок лишать вас zip'а. Раскладка каталога стала `Export/macOS/{DeveloperID,AppStore}/`, а zip остался на верхнем уровне — ровно там, где его называет `docs/release.md`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- В процессе я чуть не оставил классическую ловушку: `[ a ] || [ b ] && flag=true` под `set -euo pipefail` возвращает ненулевой статус, когда оба теста ложны, и роняет скрипт молча — то есть `--channel developer-id` завершался бы «успешно», ничего не собрав. Заменено на `case`, который всегда возвращает 0.
- Второй сюрприз был в моём тестовом харнессе, а не в коде: внешний шелл здесь **zsh**, где неэкранированный `$args` не разбивается по словам и уезжает одним аргументом. Матрица показала шесть «падений» подряд у совершенно исправного скрипта — хорошее напоминание, что при расхождении сначала подозреваем измерительный прибор.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Проверено, а не предположено:** `shellcheck` + `bash -n` чисто; матрица из 7 комбинаций флагов; `stapler validate` → «worked»; `spctl` → `accepted, source=Notarized Developer ID`; `codesign` → `flags=0x10000(runtime)`; оба билда подтверждены независимым запросом к ASC. 2. Билды загружены, но в группу тестировщиков не назначены. Группа одна — `Internal` (`8397141d-…`). Раздача людям — действие наружу, поэтому не делал сам; по слову назначу оба билда через `asc builds add-groups`.

`mise run release:ios` prints "Uploaded build N" even when xcsift has already
reported `status: incomplete`, so that line is not evidence. `xcrun altool
--list-builds` does not exist (Xcode 26.4.1 altool 26.30.4 — only upload,
validate, list-apps, list-providers). Ask the App Store Connect API instead:

```bash
mise run asc -- builds list --app 6799644194   # Hey Reachy; --limit N to trim
```

Added 2026-08-10. This replaces the hand-signed ES256 JWT script that used to be
the only way in (`uv run --with pyjwt --with cryptography …`) — `asc` signs the
token itself from the same `~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env` key, mapped onto
`ASC_*` by `Scripts/asc.sh`. Reach for the raw API only for routes `asc` lacks.

Two API details that cost a round trip each: the "What to Test" field is
`whatsNew` on `betaBuildLocalizations` (not `whatsToTest`, which 409s), and
`GET /builds/{id}/betaGroups` is forbidden — read `hasAccessToAllBuilds` on the
group instead to tell whether a build already reached the testers.

**Why:** a green exit code from the release script proves nothing, because the
xcsift pipe hides the real xcodebuild result on long runs.

**How to apply:** after any `release:ios`, read the build number and
`processingState` back from the API before telling the user it shipped.

Related: [[deploy-visual-fixes-to-device]], [[asc-cli-wiring]]

subcommand is `build-beta-detail view`, and listing/inspecting a build is
`builds info`, not `builds view`.
